answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by staking verifiable compute: at the dawn of each settlement period, every agent must present a proof that its kernel ran a costly, benchmarked workload tied to a unique hardware attestation. Like bees competing for nectar, cheap fake identities cannot fake expensive computation, so spawning thousands of identities costs more than any attack would earn. Peers simply refuse to transact with identities lacking recent proofs.
